newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends soft on pre-weekend swaps.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends soft on pre-weekend swaps.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker across the board after dealers rushed to cover short dollar positions ahead of the forthcoming long weekend on U.S. financial markets and Mexican mid-term elections, dealers said.
"Players carried some (dollar) shorts over from yesterday, and the peso was under pressure from swap trades," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended trade 3.6 and 3.0 weaker, respectively, at 7.9620/7.9650 and 7.9500/7.9550 per dollar.
"Last night's fall in (domestic) interest rates also hit the peso," the trader added.
Banco de Mexico placed bellwether 28-day Cetes at 19.95 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, a fall of 95 basis points since last week.

Dealers said several banks had chosen to exercise dollar puts with the central bank on Tuesday, and they had sold short to do so. Banco de Mexico auctions at least $300 million in dollar puts each month, which may be exercised the following month, subject to conditions.
"The market was unsettled all day and expected no relief before such a long and important weekend," a trader said.

Mexicans vote on Sunday for an new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, that post has been filled by a presidential nominee.

The outcome of the mayoral race is critical, because for the first time President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) may lose control of the nerve center of Mexico to an opposition party. The PRI has ruled Mexico for 68 unbroken years.

U.S. financial markets will close on Friday, July 4, for Independence Day, for which reason 48-hour peso contracts traded on Wednesday will not require settlement until next Monday. Dealers said this explained demand for dollars at 48 hours.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 1.1 centavos weaker at 7.9370/7.9400 per dollar.
